findings.reason: the node would add `nova` to the timing arm (or narrow the section's claim to the mounts it measures), and without that clause the section can land green while the mount its evidence names as broken is never put to the test.
findings.text: the section is titled "The why view answers on every mount within its deadline" and its own §8 record says the why view answered on no mount, yet the done-when requires only `reckon:a-project-reads-as-one-picture#s8` to answer within 30 s; `nova` is neither re-measured in the correction nor required by any arm, so §16 can close with a mount its own evidence says fails still failing

findings.reason: a writable-head against a fenced-base pair can satisfy the 30 s arm because the cache became writable rather than because the cost was removed, so the plan must re-take the base under the same writable `RECKON_HOME` (or state that it already was) before the pair can show the fix.
findings.text: the head arm requires the served why read "with a writable RECKON_HOME", but the base figure (110 s, no answer) records no cache-writability condition anywhere, and the landed record's §8 entry states "The run's write fence makes the cache read-only, so the cold timings include rebuilding the index on every call" — so the head and the base were not shown to be measured alike
